_meta.note: Fix the real issues a critical review found (verified against code), in severity order, plus two regressions I introduced this session. The review's own thesis proved out: the confident claims fell when attacked. (RV) Review integrity — the differentiator fails in BOTH directions: the Python executor FAILS OPEN (a degraded backend returns {refuted:false, findings:'<x> unavailable…'} ≥40 chars → executor.py accepts it as a 'could not refute' PASS → tag certifies an UN-reviewed state, contradicting the v1.26 guarantee); the node path FAILS CLOSED (claude-exec.sh clear path emits a canned <40-char string → hb-exec.js escalates → every review-gated run dead-ends), and verdict parse is grep REFUTED on output whose prompt contains 'REFUTED'. Fix: a degraded refute is a distinct sentinel → review_error (never a pass); the clear path carries the reviewer's real findings; robust verdict parse. Both runtimes; review acceptance is a shared behavioral surface. (RB) Robustness/parity — hb init (scaffold.py) rewrites events.jsonl UNCONDITIONALLY (node refuses without --force) → re-init wipes the append-only source of truth; gate.py runs criteria shell=True (dash) while gate.sh uses bash -c → bash-ism criteria silently diverge cross-runtime and gate.py swallows output; and my v1.27 pre-push hook is NOT self-contained — its parity proof computed the expected exit WITH PYTHONPATH but the hook runs WITHOUT it, a false-green that a stripped-env refutation would have caught. (DC) Docs↔claims — make the confident prose true: add a real .github/workflows CI running the three suites AND reword 'CI-enforced' to say exactly what enforces what; add LICENSE (MIT declared 5×, no file); fix the quickstarts that open with an unpublished `pip install heartbeat-hb`; derive the how-to index + the dev-tests T-table from source (they drifted — dev-tests stops at T116 while the suite ships T118) and gate the derivation (the T116 pattern); document the intentionally-independent plugin vs pyproject version lines. Proof-driven: spec-first, gated, refuted in a stripped env.

phases.title: Review integrity — a degraded refute must never pass; a real review must not dead-end (both runtimes)

tasks.title: Spec-first: the refute-integrity proof (both runtimes, script-stub driven)
tasks.description: Author docs/howto/gate-examples/refute-integrity.sh (prints REFUTE-INTEGRITY-OK) RED-first, driving the executor with the `script` backend + stubs (like cross-model-refuter.sh), deterministic, no model. Assert, for BOTH runtimes (node .hb/hb-exec.js and python -m heartbeat.cli/executor): (a) a DEGRADED refute (stub emits a sentinel meaning 'refuter could not run', e.g. no boolean `refuted`) does NOT advance the phase — it routes to review_error, records NO review pass, creates NO tag; (b) a GENUINE could-not-refute (stub emits refuted:false WITH substantive findings ≥40 chars) DOES pass and tags; (c) a real refutation (refuted:true) → review_failed; (d) a reviewer reply that merely echoes the instruction word 'REFUTED' inside prose but ends with the CLEAR token is NOT scored as a refutation (robust verdict parse). Must FAIL now (today the degraded path passes on python, and the node clear path dead-ends).

tasks.title: Fix the Python fail-open: degraded refute → review_error, not pass
tasks.description: Change EVERY py backend's non-verdict refute() path — both the degrade/'unavailable' path AND the 'reviewer error: {e}' exception path — across ALL of py/src/heartbeat/backends/*.py (the 7 frameworks agno/autogen/crewai/pydanticai/smolagents/langgraph/openai_agents plus any others, e.g. ollama/claude/codex/opencode) to return a distinct sentinel with NO boolean `refuted` (e.g. {"error": "<backend> unavailable (…)"}) — never a hardcoded {"refuted": false}. A genuine verdict path computes `refuted` dynamically, so the literal `"refuted": False` should remain nowhere in backends/ (this is what criterion rvd enforces). executor.py already routes a non-bool `refuted` to review_error (line ~329); make its message explicit that a degraded/unavailable refuter cannot certify a pass. Update the tests that asserted the old fail-open contract (py/tests/test_backends_frameworks.py, test_exec.py) to assert the sentinel routes to review_error and does NOT create a review pass or tag (re-assert the safe behavior — do not just delete the tests). Make refute-integrity.sh's python assertions green; keep the rest of pytest green.

tasks.title: Fix the node dead-end + fragile verdict parse
tasks.description: In plugin/templates/executors/claude-exec.sh (and the sibling bash backends): on the CLEAR path emit the reviewer's ACTUAL reply text as `findings` (so a genuine review has substantive findings and clears the ≥40 guard instead of the canned 'reviewer could not refute'); on a DEGRADE (the `claude`/backend command failed to run) emit a sentinel with no boolean `refuted` → hb-exec.js routes to review_error, not a silent pass. Make the verdict robust in claude-exec.sh AND hb-exec.js: decide REFUTED/CLEAR from the reply's final token/line, not a grep for 'REFUTED' anywhere (the prompt itself contains the word). Make refute-integrity.sh's node assertions green.

tasks.title: Wire + document the review-acceptance parity surface
tasks.description: Add group T119 (refute-integrity.sh → REFUTE-INTEGRITY-OK) to tests/run-tests.sh (marker on the same check line). Record in planning/parity-notes.md that review acceptance is a SHARED BEHAVIORAL surface (both runtimes: degraded→review_error, genuine-clear-with-substance→pass, refuted→review_failed) and that a degraded refuter is a sentinel, never a pass. Confirm node (T119 in GROUPS-PASSED), python pytest, parity, whole-docs prose all green.

Make gate-shell-parity.sh green; keep pytest + tests/parity.sh green. Document the (now closed) divergence in planning/parity-notes.md.

tasks.title: Make the pre-push hook honest + self-contained; fix its false-green proof
tasks.description: Fix the v1.27 regression: docs/howto/gate-examples/pre-push-hook-parity.sh computed the python expected-exit WITH PYTHONPATH but the hook runs WITHOUT it (false green on a box with hb installed). Make the parity proof test the hook exactly as it runs (same invocation; guard the python leg on `command -v hb` like T82.2 guards pytest). Fix the hook body (bootstrap.sh + scaffold.py) so it never blocks on an IMPORT error: node calls the always-present `.hb/gate.sh --all` (already self-contained); python requires `hb` on PATH and, if absent, prints a clear message and skips (exit 0) rather than blocking on a broken import — documented as the intentional node-vs-python difference in planning/parity-notes.md. Make pre-push-selfcontained.sh green and pre-push-hook-parity.sh honest+green.
